programme: GATA3 anchors an epithelial-differentiation programme (activating luminal/keratinocyte identity genes and restraining the Th2 cytokine set IL4/IL5/IL13 it directly transactivates) that is opposed by ZEB2-driven dedifferentiation (repressing CDH1, inducing VIM/CDH2, remodeling ECM via MMP1/MMP2) — a GATA3-vs-ZEB2 differentiation switch, with GATA3 as the only member of this pair independently placed in both tissues.
role_in_a: In breast cancer GATA3 is a well-documented luminal-differentiation and growth-suppressive factor whose stabilization or restoration blocks metastasis (USP11-GATA3, GATA3-RFPL3-ASK1 axes), while its loss is mechanistically tied to ZEB2-driven EMT and progression (MALAT1/miR-20a-5p, GPX3-ROS-TGFB1-ZEB2 axes) — i.e. GATA3 and ZEB2 sit on opposite ends of the same luminal-to-EMT transition repeatedly implicated in breast tumor progression and treatment resistance.
role_in_b: In psoriasis, GATA3 expression is reduced in lesional epidermis and is restored by narrow-band UVB phototherapy, consistent with a role in keratinocyte differentiation and in restraining the disease from an even more dedifferentiated, hyperproliferative, Th2-suppressed state. ZEB2 has no documented placement in psoriasis in this record; its role here is carried only by analogy to its breast-tissue partnership with GATA3, not by anything retrieved for skin.
shared_axis: Both breast luminal epithelium and epidermal keratinocytes depend on GATA3 to hold a differentiated, non-invasive/non-hyperproliferative state; disease in each tissue coincides with reduced or functionally suppressed GATA3, and in breast this is mechanistically coupled to de-repression of the ZEB2 dedifferentiation programme — the same differentiation-control logic recurring in two distinct epithelial compartments rather than a single documented cross-disease pathway.
reasoning: GATA3 is independently and specifically placed in both diseases (an Open Targets score in psoriasis plus a paper showing its reduction and phototherapy-induced restoration, alongside multiple mechanistic breast-cancer papers), which is enough to call the connection supported rather than merely unexpected. But the module only becomes a two-node 'switch' by adding ZEB2, which has zero psoriasis evidence in this record (no Open Targets association, no retrieved paper), so the cross-disease account rests partly on breast-cancer EMT biology extrapolated to skin rather than on anything retrieved for skin — hence moderate, not strong.
support: PMID 21611195 — shows GATA3 is decreased in psoriatic epidermis and induced by narrow-band UVB, placing GATA3 directly in disease B; PMID 42520932 — USP11 deubiquitination stabilizes GATA3 to suppress luminal breast cancer growth/metastasis; PMID 41866545 — CXCL12/ZNF503/GATA3/MMP1 axis drives TNBC progression/metastasis; PMID 41995771 — GATA3-RFPL3-ASK1 axis suppresses breast cancer growth and lung metastasis; PMID 41622408 — MALAT1/miR-20a-5p regulate ZEB2-linked EMT in breast cancer; PMID 40713734 — GPX3 promotes cisplatin resistance in TNBC via ROS-TGFB1-ZEB2.
how_to_falsify: In matched lesional vs non-lesional psoriatic skin (or keratinocyte organoids with GATA3 knockdown/restoration), test whether ZEB2 and EMT/dedifferentiation markers (loss of CDH1, gain of VIM/CDH2) move inversely with GATA3 as they do in breast epithelial models. If GATA3 loss in keratinocytes does not de-repress ZEB2 or shift these markers, the proposed differentiation-switch does not transfer to skin and the account reduces to GATA3 alone (or fails).
caveats: Tissue pairing is breast glandular epithelium vs skin epidermis — different organ systems with only a shared 'stratified/glandular epithelium' logic, not an anatomical or clinical connection. The 312 comparisons rest on only 4 independent cohort pairs, so treat the denominator as clinical-subgroup inflation, not 312 independent replications; GATA3 itself recurs in only 97/312 (~31%) of comparisons, a minority signal. ZEB2, SALL4, TCF4, ETS1, CTCFL, ONECUT2, KLF15, TCF12, MEF2C and HLX all have no Open Targets association and no retrieved literature for psoriasis — they were deliberately left out of, or (ZEB2) flagged as unsupported within, the carrying set rather than treated as evidence of novelty. MSC shows apparent cross-disease literature (PMID 41571652, 41007656, 36925706 for psoriasis), but these are about mesenchymal stem/stromal cell (MSC) exosome or secretome therapy — almost certainly a symbol collision with the transcription factor MSC/Musculin — so it was excluded from carrying_factors rather than used as support. Only a single-view exclusion list was supplied for this pair (MAML2, FOXL2, FOXF1, FOS, HIVEP3, GFI1B, VDR, CTNNB1, PBX2, PURB, KLF13, GLIS3); no tissue-generic list was given, so that check could not be applied, though no tissue master-regulator was reached for regardless.
